items.title: Wayne Shorter — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: His mother and wife, Yashodhara, they all thought, “let’s do it together.”

ctx.x: No. You know what? The world... All the universities... Now, here is something that was decreed in the world, that the Lotus Sutra... They decreed, many universities, that the Lotus Sutra was the first historic document...they call it a document...that speaks of the equality of all

people, men and women, gender, everything. Equality. Before that time, they had...back in India, the men had 500-and-something sins and some other things that they had to overcome, and women had 2,500, and a woman can never be enlightened until she comes reborn as a man and all that. So then Shakyamuni came along and said, “To hell with that! Unh-uh. That ain’t that way at all.” But I liked that. I said, “Wait a minute. He didn’t write nothing down.” In the moment, when it happened to him... It happened to him…
What do you think the answer to that question is?
